meta.aciklama:
Scaling AI agents across multiple software repositories usually means copy-pasting prompts and workflows. warpdotdev/common-skills solves this by creating a standardized catalog of reusable agent skills.

Structured under .agents/skills/, each skill contains clear YAML frontmatter, helper scripts, and documentation. Built-in workflows handle spec drafting, PR risk evaluation, local diff reviews, CI failure diagnosis, subagent research delegation, and cross-critique routines. It even includes skill-doctor, which grades existing skills using actual local agent conversations to recommend targeted upgrades.

You can easily distribute global or project-specific agent behaviors using the npx skills CLI.

Check out warpdotdev/common-skills on GitHub to streamline your agentic developer workflows!

transkript.t: Imagine giving your AI agents a standardized playbook of reusable software engineering skills across all your repos.
That's what Warp's Common Skills Repository does.
It uses a structured agent skills format installable directly via NPX.
Instead of reinventing prompts for every project, it gives your coding agents modular pre-built capabilities.
You get skills for writing tech specs, diagnosing CI failures, assessing PR merge risk, and resolving Git conflicts.
It even includes sub-agent cross-critique for complex decisions and a skill doctor tool that audits chat logs to refine agent behavior.
Check out warp.dev.com and skills on GitHub to see how it works.
